title: sdk-onboard-feedback-loop-notebook
body:
Purpose:
This is a working notebook for a small experiment: pair compact SDK quickstarts with an explicit feedback loop and lightweight telemetry so we can iterate documentation, sample code, and error messaging faster.

Background / motivation:
- We ship lots of short SDK starter docs. We often only learn about friction after customers hit support or churn.
- Idea: make the onboarding docs themselves both instructive and diagnostic. Collect opt-in, privacy-friendly signals to identify high-friction steps and surface them to docs authors + SDK owners.
- Focus on the first 30 minutes: account set-up, API key, run-first-request, parse-response, handle-errors.

Primary goals:
1) Reduce time-to-first-success (TTFS) by 25% in experiment cohort.
2) Surface top 3 pain points (by funnel drop-off + error rate) from real users within 2 weeks of publish.
3) Create 3 small lab templates that non-engineers (product managers, solutions) can run in a 30–60 minute session with a teammate.

Non-goals:
- Not trying to replace product analytics. Keep telemetry tiny and privacy-preserving.
- Not an enterprise-grade audit trail; this is early experiments.

Design outline (high level):
A) Instructional artifact: "Starter Lab (30m)" package
  - 2 short lab scripts: "Hello API", "Context + Summarize"
  - Minimal code (Python + JS versions) with 6–8 lines to run the first request
  - A checklist for success: valid API key, 200 response, expected token count approx
  - Persona notes: dev vs PM vs solutions engineer (what each should verify)

B) Instrumentation (opt-in, minimal):
  - On the quickstart page, an explicit opt-in toggle: "Share anonymous troubleshooting signals for 14 days"
  - If opted-in, the starter lab calls a tiny telemetry endpoint with: step-id, sdk-language, success/failure, short error code, time-to-complete (ms). No request/response body, no user prompt text, no model output.
  - Store aggregated metrics per-doc: funnel counts, median TTFS, top error codes.
  - Add a lightweight session-id cookie to tie events together while the opt-in is active.

C) Error capture patterns to help docs authors (example signals):
  - auth-invalid-token
  - network-timeout
  - model-compatibility-mismatch (client asked for model X but server redirected)
  - response-parse-error
  - usage-quota-exceeded

D) Dashboard & alerts (developer-experience view):
  - Per-lab heatmap: step completion rate over last 14 days
  - Rolling list of top error codes (95th percentiles for times)
  - Quick link to draft edit for the doc, plus suggested copy changes (templated)
  - Weekly digest email for owners with top 3 flagged docs

Lab templates (short outlines):
1) Hello-API (10–15 minutes)
  - Objective: Make a successful generation call, print text, handle 401/403
  - Steps: create key, set env var, run python script, inspect 200, print output, optional stream mode
  - Validation: script exits 0, prints "Success" + sample token count

2) Context-Summarize (30 minutes)
  - Objective: send a multi-turn context, request a concise summary, handle length truncation
  - Steps: run starter app with local file input, confirm model returns JSON or structured output, show how to set max tokens / temperature
  - Validation: output contains the phrase "summary:" and length < 400 tokens

3) Error-Handling Playbook (20 minutes)
  - Objective: intentionally trigger common failure modes and show best-retry/backoff patterns
  - Steps: simulate 429 by throttling, simulate 500 with mock endpoint, verify exponential backoff works, show client-side idempotency guard for duplicate requests
  - Validation: all retries succeed or timeout gracefully with actionable error message

Measurement plan (how to decide success):
- TTFS: measure time from lab page load to first successful call (opt-in users only).
- Completion funnel: page load -> copy key -> run script -> success
- Error ratio: opt-in sessions that reported an error event / total sessions
- Qualitative: optional follow-up micro-survey (1 question) at end of lab: "Did this get you to a working call?" (yes/no) + freeform (optional)

Privacy & compliance notes:
- No prompt text, no model output collected. Hash or zero-record for any identifiers beyond session id. TTL 14 days, automatic delete.
- Doc explicitly shows how to opt-out and how to delete your session history.
- Need sign-off from privacy/security before rolling beyond internal beta.

Runbook for an experiment release (quick steps):
- Draft lab + code samples in GH repo (small PR) -> add telemetry hook flag behind feature toggle -> internal beta with ~50 users (solutions + sales engineers) -> run 2-week collection -> review dashboard -> iterate doc (copy/code) -> repeat.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Which events should we consider PII? (session id, IP) -> flag for security team.
- Exact sampling rate: all opt-ins vs 1:5 sampling to lower noise?
- UX for opt-in: banner vs modal vs inline checkbox (A/B test)
- Who maintains the dashboard? product-ops or developer-experience?

Notes to self / rough tasks:
- [ ] Prototype Hello-API lab (python/js) — Priya (due: 2025-10-01)
- [ ] Backend telemetry stub + retention policy — Evan (due: 2025-10-08)
- [ ] Dashboard mock in Figma + email digest mockup — Marina (due: 2025-10-15)
- [ ] Privacy review meeting invite — Samir (this week)
- [ ] Recruit 4 internal volunteers for beta: solutions, pm, growth, eng (ask on #dev-experience)

Quick draft of user-facing copy (for the top of the lab page):
"Get started in 30 minutes: Run a short sample, see a result. Opt-in to anonymous troubleshooting signals to help us improve this guide — we do not collect your prompts or model outputs."

Closing thought: keep the first experiment tiny and observable. If we can reduce a single common friction (auth or missing env vars) and capture it reliably, we can ship a lot of small UX wins fast.
